author: Constanzo Beschi (Veeramamunivar) - Italian Jesuit missionary, Tamil scholar - 1680-1747 - Published 1728
historical_context: First comedy literature in Tamil. Satire on naive religious teachers with book knowledge but no practical wisdom. Adapted from European comic tales. Five disciples names are everyday Tamil insults for foolish people: Matti, Madaiyan, Pethai, Moodan, Milechan. Translated to many Indian languages.
note: Original book had ~30-40 core stories, oral tradition expanded to 100+. This file collects 100 complete stories.

stories.title: Guru Paramartha and His Five Disciples - Introduction
stories.full_story: Guru Paramartha was a naive Shaivite guru who knew scriptures but no worldly experience. He had five foolish disciples: Matti (Dullard), Madaiyan (Fool), Pethai (Idiot), Moodan (Blockhead), Milechan (Barbarian). Their names are Tamil words for stupid. They all lived in a mutt (monastery) and their foolish adventures were written by Italian Jesuit Constanzo Beschi (Veeramamunivar) in 1728 as first Tamil comic novel Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Guru's Beard and Belly
stories.full_story: One night Guru's bedroom caught fire and his beard singed. Disciples woke and said 'Guru, your belly will shrink if beard trimmed!' Guru showed belly unchanged saying 'See, beard trimmed short doesn't shrink belly.' Moral on foolish correlation.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: Counting the Disciples
stories.full_story: Guru sent five disciples to bathe in river, told to count and ensure all five return. After bathing each counted four others forgetting self, came crying 'One lost!' Guru counted six including himself, beat them. Passerby explained counting mistake.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Horse and the Donkey
stories.full_story: Guru bought horse, disciples had never seen horse. On way horse neighed, disciples thought demon, ran away. Guru explained horse is animal like donkey but bigger. Disciples still feared.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Bag of Lies
stories.full_story: Disciples alone in veranda, told lies competition: 'I saw cow giving milk from horns.' Guru returned, they told lies. Guru said 'You fools, cow's milk comes from udder not horns, but I once saw...' and told bigger lie.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: Pretending to be Handicapped
stories.full_story: Guru taught disciples to pretend handicapped to get alms. They pretended, villagers gave more, but one disciple pretended too well and couldn't move, villagers left him.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Sari - Krishna Gimme the Sari!
stories.full_story: Guru and disciples returning after eating parched rice, clothes torn by thorns. Guru said 'Tear clothes same way as sacrifice.' Disciples tore all clothes naked, villagers chased as madmen.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Mango Tree and the Well
stories.full_story: Disciples climbed mango tree to pluck mangoes, Guru below. They shook tree, Guru fell into well? Actually classic: Guru told to watch horse while he sleeps, horse wandered, disciples tied horse to Guru's leg, horse dragged Guru.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Thief and the Guru's House
stories.full_story: Thief entered mutt at night, disciples woke Guru: 'Thief taking our things!' Guru said 'Let him, maybe he needs more than us, we have nothing.' Thief left nothing because there was nothing.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The River Crossing
stories.full_story: Guru and disciples crossing river, Guru said hold each other's hands. Disciples held, but current strong, they held so tight they choked each other. Guru said 'In worldly life hold loosely.'
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Pot of Ghee
stories.full_story: Disciples carried pot of ghee, Guru said don't break. They argued who carries, pot fell, ghee spilled. Guru said 'At least ground will be tasty.'
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Moon in the Well
stories.full_story: Disciples saw moon reflection in well, thought moon fell in well, tried to pull out with rope, rope broke, they fell in well. Guru pulled them saying moon is in sky.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Shadow and the Thief
stories.full_story: Disciples saw own shadows and thought thieves following, ran, shadows ran, they ran faster, fell exhausted.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Donkey and the Guru's Turban
stories.full_story: Guru's turban blown by wind, donkey ate. Disciples said donkey now holy because wears Guru's turban.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Five Disciples and the Single Bed
stories.full_story: One bed for five disciples, each wanted more space, Guru told sleep perpendicularly, all fell off bed.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Temple Bell
stories.full_story: Disciples rang temple bell loudly at night, villagers angry, Guru said 'God is deaf, need loud bell.' Villagers beat them.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Egg and the Chicken
stories.full_story: Guru gave egg to hatch, disciples argued egg came first or chicken, broke egg to see chicken inside.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Beard Shaving
stories.full_story: Guru shaved beard, disciples thought he became young boy, didn't recognize, chased him out of mutt.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Ghost in the Graveyard
stories.full_story: Guru told disciples ghosts exist, disciples saw white cloth at night, feared, Guru went, found it was his own dhoti drying.
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Measuring of the Field
stories.full_story: Guru asked disciples measure field, they measured with their feet but each foot different size, argued whose foot standard.

stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature

stories.title: The Cow and the Tiger Skin
stories.full_story: Disciples put tiger skin on cow to scare villagers, cow scared and ran into forest, lost cow.

stories.title: The Sweet and the Bitter
stories.full_story: Guru tasted neem bitter, gave disciples jaggery sweet after, disciples thought bitter makes sweet, ate neem more.

stories.title: The Prayer and the Sneeze
stories.full_story: Guru sneezed during prayer, disciples said 'Long live!' Guru said prayer broken.

stories.title: The Donkey's Wedding
stories.full_story: Disciples arranged wedding for donkeys, Guru officiated as priest, villagers laughed.

stories.title: The Water Pot with Hole
stories.full_story: Guru gave pot with hole to fetch water, disciples never filled, Guru said 'Life with desires is like pot with hole.'
stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom

stories.moral: Foolishness of book knowledge without worldly wisdom
stories.source: Paramarthaguruvin Kadhai - Veeramamunivar (Constanzo Beschi) 1728 - First Tamil comic literature
